claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the distinguished-point Pollard rho walk described in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.3935 (birthday 1-exp(-1/2)) using at most 2^128.1 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, failures, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^119 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^12 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes. The non-reference walk overhead is bounded at 64 scalar instructions per step (0.064 reference equivalents), a tighter charge than the 0.5H bound of the sibling candidate. This is a classical cold generic attack whose only heuristic assumption is the standard Pollard rho birthday collision (disclosed in proof.md). It is a supported sqrt(r) generic frontier estimate, not a novel sub-exponential or structural break, not a practical production execution, and not a weakened-hardness claim.

experiments.purpose: Run a real Pollard rho (full-table) on prime-order subgroups of small multiplicative groups Z_n^* to exercise the sector-mixing walk, collision extraction, log-vector arithmetic and verification (falling back to exhaustive search only for the degenerate q < 64 subgroups). It does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
